sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 133, recorded on June 6, 2023.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 133 期，录制于 2023 年 6 月 6 日。

sentences.en: My name is Conor, and on today's episode, we interview attendees and speakers from the Lambda Days 2023 conference that took place on June 5th to June 6th in Krakow, Poland.
sentences.zh: 我是 Conor，在今天的节目中，我们将采访 2023 年 6 月 5 日至 6 日在波兰克拉科夫举行的 Lambda Days 2023 大会的参会者和演讲者。

sentences.en: We interview, in this episode, Toby Pfeiffer, Kim Huizing, Alexis King, Jose Valim, Andor Pens, and Pierre Stritzinger.
sentences.zh: 本期节目我们采访了 Toby Pfeiffer、Kim Huizing、Alexis King、Jose Valim、Andor Pens 和 Pierre Stritzinger。

sentences.en: This is part one of a two-part episode.
sentences.zh: 这是两集系列节目的第一部分。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: First time we're ever doing a live interview on ADSP, the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这是我们 ADSP 播客第一次进行现场采访。

sentences.en: We're here with Toby Pfeiffer.
sentences.zh: 我们现在和 Toby Pfeiffer 在一起。

sentences.en: Toby, I mean, I know where you're from and what communities you operate in, but the people do not.
sentences.zh: Toby，我知道你来自哪里，也知道你在哪些社区活跃，但听众们不知道。

sentences.en: Introduce yourself briefly.
sentences.zh: 简单介绍一下你自己吧。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Toby.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫 Toby。

sentences.en: I'm from Berlin in Germany.
sentences.zh: 我来自德国柏林。

sentences.en: I'm mostly active in the Elixir community.
sentences.zh: 我主要活跃在 Elixir 社区。

sentences.en: I'm known for Benchy there, which is like the benchmarking library, and otherwise operate in the Ruby community a lot.
sentences.zh: 我在那里因为 Benchy（一个基准测试库）而闻名，此外我也经常在 Ruby 社区活动。

sentences.en: I maintain SimpleCov, which is a code coverage library, and I run the Ruby user group in Berlin for like almost 11 years.
sentences.zh: 我维护着 SimpleCov（一个代码覆盖率库），并且经营柏林的 Ruby 用户组已经快 11 年了。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, that's what I do.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这就是我的工作。

sentences.en: So you went from Ruby to Elixir.
sentences.zh: 所以你是从 Ruby 转到了 Elixir。

sentences.en: Why the switch?
sentences.zh: 为什么要转呢？

sentences.en: Should everyone in Ruby switch to Elixir?
sentences.zh: 每个人都应该从 Ruby 转到 Elixir 吗？

sentences.en: Although you still operate in both communities.
sentences.zh: 尽管你现在仍然活跃在这两个社区。

sentences.en: It's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: Not everybody should switch, but like I personally...
sentences.zh: 并不是每个人都应该转，但我个人……

sentences.en: Ruby is a lot of like very fancy stuff, very fancy metaprogramming, very many things that go haywire.
sentences.zh: Ruby 有很多非常花哨的东西，非常花哨的元编程，还有很多容易出乱子的东西。

sentences.en: And especially, let's say, I don't want to start a flame war, although somebody told me that's good for viewership.
sentences.zh: 特别是，怎么说呢，我不想引发口水战，尽管有人告诉我这对收视率有好处。

sentences.en: Yeah, start a flame war if you want.
sentences.zh: 没关系，想引发口水战就引发吧。

sentences.en: Go for it.
sentences.zh: 尽管来。

sentences.en: So Rails, and especially ActiveRecord, has a lot of this magic going on with all of those callbacks going back and forth, back and forth.
sentences.zh: Rails，尤其是 ActiveRecord，有很多这种魔法，各种回调来回穿梭。

sentences.en: And so it's so hard to figure out where a buck is.
sentences.zh: 所以很难找出 Bug 在哪里。

sentences.en: And like I saw Elixir and like the function programming paradigm and also the way that they designed, for instance, their database layer,
sentences.zh: 当我看到 Elixir 以及函数式编程范式，还有他们设计数据库层的方式时，比如……

sentences.en: Acto, as being much more explicit about what happens.
sentences.zh: Ecto，它对发生的事情要明确得多。

sentences.en: So like in Acto, you got to go and you actually have a repo instance.
sentences.zh: 在 Ecto 中，你必须去操作一个 Repo 实例。

sentences.en: And every time you make a query to the database, you actually got to go to the repo and be like, repo, do this thing.
sentences.zh: 每次你向数据库查询时，你都必须去调用 Repo，就像说：Repo，做这件事。

sentences.en: And so it's very explicit, like where SQL queries happen and all of that.
sentences.zh: 所以 SQL 查询在哪里发生是非常明确的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And I just enjoyed that and the architecture and the thinking, you know, much more.
sentences.zh: 我只是更喜欢这种架构和思维方式。

sentences.en: And plus, Ruby is still not great at, you know, parallel programming.
sentences.zh: 另外，Ruby 在并行编程方面仍然不太擅长。

sentences.en: Like Ruby has now guilds and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 虽然 Ruby 现在有了 Guilds 之类的东西。

sentences.en: But like, you know, it's the year of like 2023, right?
sentences.zh: 但现在已经是 2023 年了，对吧？

sentences.en: And, you know, Elixir and Erlang, like the Acto model is just so great.
sentences.zh: 而且，Elixir 和 Erlang 的 Actor 模型真是太棒了。

sentences.en: And I always wanted to work with the Acto model.
sentences.zh: 我一直想使用 Actor 模型工作。

sentences.en: And like Elixir gave me that nice way into it that's not as hardcore as Erlang.
sentences.zh: Elixir 为我提供了一种很好的切入方式，不像 Erlang 那么硬核。

sentences.en: It's like a little bit of Ruby, a little bit of like the Ruby abstractions, let's say.
sentences.zh: 它有一点 Ruby 的影子，或者说有一点 Ruby 的抽象。

sentences.en: But I can still use the full power of the Beam VM, which I'm very happy about.
sentences.zh: 但我仍然可以使用 BEAM 虚拟机的所有强大功能，对此我非常高兴。

sentences.en: But it's a great conference.

sentences.en: And what I love about it is that, you know, all of the different languages go together here.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它的一点是，各种不同的语言在这里汇聚一堂。

sentences.en: Because sometimes I say, you know, I've been to so many Ruby conferences.

sentences.en: But then it's so cool for me to go watch like a Haskell talk or go watch a Clojure talk and see like how does this community think?
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，去听一场 Haskell 演讲或 Clojure 演讲，看看这个社区是怎么思考的，真是太酷了。

sentences.en: So, for instance, one thing that I've also heard you say yesterday is that, you know, from the Clojure community, I learned to focus on data.
sentences.zh: 比如，昨天我听到你说，从 Clojure 社区，我学会了专注于数据。

sentences.en: You know, it's all about data.

sentences.en: And that changed the way I think about programming.
sentences.zh: 这改变了我对编程的思考方式。

sentences.en: And so, I love going out there and like taking bits and pieces from other communities to change the way that I think about programming.
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢走出去，从其他社区汲取点滴，来改变我对编程的思考方式。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.

sentences.zh: 人们可以从你刚才的演讲中期待些什么？

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: So, the talk is titled Stories in Open Source.
sentences.zh: 演讲的标题是《开源中的故事》。

sentences.en: And it goes, basically goes through my story in open source.
sentences.zh: 它基本上讲述了我在开源领域的故事。

sentences.en: Like how I started out in open source and was very frustrating.
sentences.zh: 比如我刚开始做开源时是多么令人沮丧。

sentences.en: And it talks about why was it frustrating?
sentences.zh: 它谈到了为什么会令人沮丧？

sentences.en: What was bad?
sentences.zh: 哪里不好？

sentences.en: And then how I finally got into open source.
sentences.zh: 然后我是如何最终进入开源领域的。

sentences.en: What worked for me and sort of like all the benefits I took from that.
sentences.zh: 什么对我有效，以及我从中获得的所有好处。

sentences.en: But also what I learned about like open source project management or like also just in general
sentences.zh: 但也谈到了我学到的关于开源项目管理，或者更广泛地说……

sentences.en: working with people and tries to tell the story and give people a good piece of knowledge and advice so that they can either sort of like maintain the open source projects better,
sentences.zh: 与人合作的经验，试图讲述这个故事并给人们一些好的知识和建议，这样他们可以更好地维护开源项目，

sentences.en: contribute to open source projects, or like essentially also whatever other sort of like volunteer work they do, just have a better time doing it.
sentences.zh: 为开源项目做贡献，或者本质上做任何其他志愿工作时，都能有更好的体验。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was awesome talk.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是一场很棒的演讲。

sentences.en: Can definitely recommend.
sentences.zh: 绝对值得推荐。

sentences.en: I mean, there's so many highlights.

sentences.en: One of my favorite points that you made, though, is that, you know, people mistake your sort of expertise in the Beam, which is the VM that, for those that don't know, that, you
sentences.zh: 不过，你提到的我最喜欢的观点之一是，人们误解了你在 BEAM 方面的专业知识——对于那些不知道的人，BEAM 是……

sentences.en: know, languages like Elixir and Erlang run on.
sentences.zh: Elixir 和 Erlang 等语言运行的虚拟机。

sentences.en: They figured, oh, like you must have been an expert before you started building Benchy.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，哦，你在开始构建 Benchy 之前一定就是专家了。

sentences.en: Anyways, I'll let you finish the rest because that was one of my favorite parts.
sentences.zh: 总之，剩下的部分我就让你自己讲了，因为那是我最喜欢的部分之一。

sentences.en: It's like, that's a great learning lesson for folks that are, you know, want to get to that level, but think, oh, it's, you know, I'm not an expert.
sentences.zh: 这对于那些想达到那个水平，但又觉得“哦，我不是专家”的人来说，是一个很好的教训。

sentences.en: So, yeah, essentially people, you know, come up and it's like, oh, you need to, you need to have known all of this about it.
sentences.zh: 所以，本质上人们会走过来问，哦，你一定早就知道所有这些了。

sentences.en: And like, it's like, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 而事实是，不，不，不。

sentences.en: So, you know, the relationship is inverse.
sentences.zh: 关系是反过来的。

sentences.en: I didn't know anything about it, but I started writing this benchmarking library and in order
sentences.zh: 我对此一无所知，但我开始编写这个基准测试库，为了……

sentences.en: to write it and write it well, I needed to learn about the Beam, and that's why I became so good at knowing it.
sentences.zh: 把它写好，我需要学习 BEAM，这就是我变得如此精通的原因。

sentences.en: So, that's both, you know, how time measurements work, how processes and memory measurement work.
sentences.zh: 所以，这包括时间测量是如何工作的，进程和内存测量是如何工作的。

sentences.en: So, for instance, there's a very fun story where, like, we tried to introduce memory measurements

sentences.en: in Benchy.
sentences.zh: 看看我运行的这个函数到底消耗了多少内存。

sentences.en: So, like, see, like, how much memory consumption does this one function that I take, that I run take, basically.

sentences.en: And if you're interested in that, my co-maintainer, Devin Estes, actually gave a very great talk about that very many times about, like, how memory measurement works in the Beam.
sentences.zh: 那只是我们做这项工作并弄清楚它之后的结果。

sentences.en: And that was just the result of us, you know, doing that work and figuring that out.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常有趣。

sentences.en: And so, it's very fun.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想学点什么，就去动手做吧。

sentences.en: So, like, yeah, if you want to learn something, you know, go work on it.

sentences.zh: 在 IMG，我主要用 Scala 工作，也会处理一些杂七杂八的任务。

sentences.en: I have a passion for RegEx and AWK.
sentences.zh: 我对正则表达式（RegEx）和 AWK 情有独钟。

sentences.en: And I do a bit of infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 我也会做一点基础设施方面的工作。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Just various things to keep busy.
sentences.zh: 就是各种各样的事情，让自己忙起来。

sentences.en: But yeah.
sentences.zh: 不过确实。

sentences.en: Scala is my bread and butter.
sentences.zh: Scala 是我的看家本领。

sentences.en: If you had to recommend people between checking out Scala or AWK, you know.
sentences.zh: 如果让你推荐大家去了解 Scala 还是 AWK，你知道的。

sentences.en: And what do you love about AWK?
sentences.zh: 你为什么喜欢 AWK？

sentences.en: Why is that one of your personal passions?
sentences.zh: 为什么那是你的个人爱好之一？

sentences.en: Because it's super, super faSt.
sentences.zh: 因为它超级、超级快。

sentences.en: And it combines some of my favorite things, which are words and logic.
sentences.zh: 而且它结合了我最喜欢的两样东西：文字和逻辑。

sentences.en: So what's better, Scala or AWK?
sentences.zh: 那么哪个更好，Scala 还是 AWK？

sentences.en: If you only had to choose one, or if you had to recommend folks to go check out a language, which one do you recommend?
sentences.zh: 如果只能选一个，或者如果必须向大家推荐一门语言去学习，你会推荐哪一个？

sentences.en: I would recommend Scala, because you can do everything with Scala.
sentences.zh: 我会推荐 Scala，因为你可以用 Scala 做任何事情。

sentences.en: You cannot do everything with AWK.
sentences.zh: 你不能用 AWK 做所有事情。

sentences.en: But yeah, for certain things, it can be really good.
sentences.zh: 但确实，对于某些特定任务，它非常出色。

sentences.en: And especially if you want to do some data manipulation in the cloud or something, it's a very good choice.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果你想在云端进行一些数据处理之类的操作，它是一个非常好的选择。

sentences.en: Awesome.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And is this your first time attending Lambda Days, or have you been here before?
sentences.zh: 这是你第一次参加 Lambda Days，还是以前来过？

sentences.en: It's my first time here.
sentences.zh: 这是我第一次来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: You think you'll be back?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你还会再来吗？

sentences.en: I think I will.
sentences.zh: 我想我会的。

sentences.en: Awesome.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thanks for being on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 感谢你参加这次播客。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: We are here with Alexis King, closing keynote of day one of Lambda Days 2023.
sentences.zh: 我们现在和 Alexis King 在一起，她是 2023 年 Lambda Days 第一天的闭幕主讲人。

sentences.en: Introduce yourself, because most of the listeners probably operate in the system space.
sentences.zh: 请自我介绍一下，因为大多数听众可能是在系统领域工作的。

sentences.en: So some people know who you are, even though you're very well known in the Haskell community.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人知道你是谁，尽管你在 Haskell 社区非常出名。

sentences.en: So introduce sort of where you're from, what you're working on, and maybe we'll talk a bit about the keynote that you gave yesterday, which was awesome, by the way.
sentences.zh: 简单介绍一下你来自哪里，正在做什么，也许我们可以聊聊你昨天做的那个主讲，顺便说一下，那场演讲太棒了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: You're just, I feel like I'm talking to a news reporter.
sentences.zh: 你真是……我觉得我像是在接受新闻记者采访。

sentences.en: But yeah, I'm Alexis King.
sentences.zh: 不过，我是 Alexis King。

sentences.en: I work for a company called Tweak at the moment, and I work on GHC, Haskell Compiler.
sentences.zh: 目前我在一家叫 Tweak 的公司工作，负责 GHC（Haskell 编译器）的相关工作。

sentences.en: And currently, I've been working on improving the compile time performance of GHC.
sentences.zh: 目前，我一直致力于提高 GHC 的编译时间性能。

sentences.en: But I've also, in the past, which I was speaking on today, was delimited continuations.
sentences.zh: 但我过去也做过一些研究，也就是我今天演讲的主题：定界延续（delimited continuations）。

sentences.en: I've added delimited continuations to the GHC RTS, which is exciting.
sentences.zh: 我为 GHC RTS 添加了定界延续功能，这很令人兴奋。

sentences.en: Of course, it probably doesn't mean very much to most people, because delimited continuations are a mystery to most people.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对大多数人来说可能意义不大，因为定界延续对大多数人来说是个谜。

sentences.en: But that's the whole reason I gave this talk.
sentences.zh: 但这正是我想做这场演讲的原因。

sentences.en: So if you're interested, you can watch the talk.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你感兴趣，可以去看看那场演讲。

sentences.en: The talk was absolutely phenomenal.
sentences.zh: 那场演讲简直太精彩了。

sentences.en: We'll talk about how beautiful the slides were in a second.
sentences.zh: 我们待会儿再聊聊那些幻灯片有多美。

sentences.en: But give people maybe, I'm not even sure, is it possible to give like a 30-second overview of what people can expect from this amazing delimited continuations talk?
sentences.zh: 但能不能给听众们，我甚至不确定，能不能用 30 秒概括一下大家可以从这场关于定界延续的精彩演讲中期待些什么？

sentences.en: Because not only was it beautiful, but I think it's probably going to be the most approachable talk.
sentences.zh: 因为它不仅精美，而且我认为它可能是最平易近人的演讲。

sentences.en: Not that there's been too many talks given on delimited continuations.
sentences.zh: 并不是说关于定界延续的演讲已经有很多了。

sentences.en: But what can, maybe a 30-second high level as best you can?
sentences.zh: 但你能尽量用 30 秒做一个高层级的概述吗？

sentences.en: Because it's a hairy topic to try and summarize in a little podcast bite.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个很难在简短的播客片段中总结的复杂话题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, I think really the sort of core concept that delimited continuations are really about is this ability to suspend and then later resume computations.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为定界延续的核心概念实际上是关于挂起计算并在稍后恢复计算的能力。

sentences.en: And the sort of discussion of exactly how that happens is complicated.
sentences.zh: 关于这究竟是如何发生的讨论很复杂。

sentences.en: But the talk goes into the detail and sort of perhaps at times painfully exquisite detail about exactly how that happens.
sentences.zh: 但演讲深入探讨了细节，甚至有时是极其细致入微的细节，解释了这一切究竟是如何发生的。

sentences.en: But the interesting thing about it is that you can use them to implement all these common
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，你可以利用它们来实现所有这些常见的

sentences.en: types of weird fancy control operators that show up in programming languages like generators, coroutines, exceptions, and that's really what they're about.
sentences.zh: 奇怪而高级的控制运算符，这些运算符出现在编程语言中，比如生成器、协程、异常，这才是它们真正的意义所在。

sentences.en: Awesome.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So, we will link your keynote.
sentences.zh: 我们会附上你的主讲链接。

sentences.en: I'm not actually sure.
sentences.zh: 我其实不太确定。

sentences.en: I think, if I remember correctly, the Lambda Days 2022 talks, they took a few months to come out.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，Lambda Days 2022 的演讲视频过了几个月才发布。

sentences.en: I think it was four to six months.
sentences.zh: 我想大概是四到六个月。

sentences.en: So, unfortunately, folks are listening to this in the middle of June.
sentences.zh: 所以很遗憾，大家听到这期节目时正值六月中旬。

sentences.en: Actually, I will be giving the talk again in about a week at ZuriHack.
sentences.zh: 其实，我大约一周后会在 ZuriHack 再做一次演讲。

sentences.en: And I think the ZuriHack talks, they normally get them up pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 我想 ZuriHack 的演讲视频通常发布得很快。

sentences.en: So, maybe you can link that one.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许你可以链接那一个。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: ZuriHack, that's Zed or Z, depending on what country you're in, U-R-I, so like the first four letters of Zurich, and then Hack, H-A-C.
sentences.zh: ZuriHack，那是 Z-U-R-I，就像苏黎世（Zurich）的前四个字母，然后是 Hack，H-A-C。

sentences.en: I didn't even know this existed, and I'm a pretty prolific talk watcher.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道它的存在，而我还是个相当多产的演讲视频观看者。

sentences.en: Tell us a little bit, what is ZuriHack?
sentences.zh: 给我们介绍一下，什么是 ZuriHack？

sentences.en: How come I didn't know about it?
sentences.zh: 为什么我不知道它？

sentences.en: And what can people expect from this kind of conference?
sentences.zh: 人们对这种会议有什么期待？

sentences.en: It's free, right?
sentences.zh: 它是免费的，对吧？

sentences.en: It is free.
sentences.zh: 确实是免费的。

sentences.en: So, how do you know that it's free if you didn't know about it?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你之前不知道它，你是怎么知道它是免费的？

sentences.en: I found out this morning from Meow.
sentences.zh: 我今天早上从 Meow 那里得知的。

sentences.en: Hope you're listening, Meow.
sentences.zh: 希望你在听，Meow。

sentences.en: Meow, I'm not actually sure I'm pronouncing that exactly correct, but Meow said, it's a shame you're not going to ZuriHack, because you've flown all the way over here from Toronto,
sentences.zh: Meow，我不确定我发音是否完全正确，但 Meow 说，你不去 ZuriHack 太可惜了，因为你都从多伦多飞到这里了，

sentences.en: Canada.
sentences.zh: 加拿大。

sentences.en: And then it was in that moment that I realized, I'm actually flying to Zurich on Sunday, and
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻我意识到，我周日确实要飞往苏黎世，

sentences.en: I'm taking a week off of vacation, and I'm going to be in Switzerland for a week, the first two days of which, Sunday and Monday, I will be in Zurich.
sentences.zh: 我请了一周假，要在瑞士待一周，前两天，也就是周日和周一，我会在苏黎世。

sentences.en: So, serendipitously, and I was like, is it too late to sign up?
sentences.zh: 所以，真是机缘巧合，我当时就问，现在报名还来得及吗？

sentences.en: And he said, it's free.
sentences.zh: 他说，它是免费的。

sentences.en: So, that's how I know it's free.
sentences.zh: 所以我才知道它是免费的。

sentences.en: So, maybe I'll see you at ZuriHack.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许我会在 ZuriHack 见到你。

sentences.en: But yes, I have no idea what the conference is about.
sentences.zh: 但确实，我不知道这个会议是关于什么的。

sentences.en: I learned about it yesterday, and I learned that it was free this morning.
sentences.zh: 我昨天才知道它，今天早上才知道它是免费的。

sentences.en: So, tell the listeners what they can expect from the conference.
sentences.zh: 那么，告诉听众们他们可以从这个会议中期待些什么。

sentences.en: All right, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: So, I mean, it's sort of a hybrid.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它算是一种混合形式。

sentences.en: People give some talks, but then there's also like a hackathon component, which is the hack part of ZuriHack.
sentences.zh: 人们会做一些演讲，但也有黑客马拉松的部分，这就是 ZuriHack 的“Hack”部分。

sentences.en: And normally people, I mean, it's pretty casual.
sentences.zh: 通常人们，嗯，它相当随意。

sentences.en: I actually have never been in person.
sentences.zh: 我其实从来没有亲自参加过。

sentences.en: I spoke at it three years ago, which was when I signed up.
sentences.zh: 我三年前在上面讲过话，那是我报名的时候。

sentences.en: I was going to be in person, but then something happened.
sentences.zh: 我本来打算亲自参加的，但后来发生了一些事。

sentences.en: So, I didn't.
sentences.zh: 所以我没去成。

sentences.en: So, I'm excited to be there.
sentences.zh: 所以我很期待能去那里。

sentences.en: But my understanding is that it's normally pretty chill.
sentences.zh: 但据我了解，它通常相当轻松。

sentences.en: People will just kind of propose some projects.
sentences.zh: 人们会提出一些项目。

sentences.en: You can pitch in if you want.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，可以参与其中。

sentences.en: You can do your own thing.
sentences.zh: 你也可以做你自己的事情。

sentences.en: Just chat with people.
sentences.zh: 就是和大家聊天。

sentences.en: I'll probably honestly spend a lot of the time just talking to people.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我可能会花很多时间只是和人交谈。

sentences.en: But it should be fun.
sentences.zh: 但这应该会很有趣。

sentences.en: There's also a few people presenting, obviously myself included.
sentences.zh: 当然也有一些人会做演讲，显然包括我自己。

sentences.en: And, yeah, it should just be a pleasant time.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，这应该会是一段愉快的时光。

sentences.en: Lastly, maybe I'll ask, you've given a ton of talks in the past at a plethora of conferences, many of them, you know, highly regarded on the interwebs.
sentences.zh: 最后，我可能想问一下，你过去在众多会议上做过大量的演讲，其中许多在互联网上备受推崇。

sentences.en: Is there a place people can sort of find all of your talks or if they want to follow you on socials?
sentences.zh: 有没有一个地方可以让人们找到你所有的演讲，或者如果他们想在社交媒体上关注你？

sentences.en: Like, what's the best way to sort of follow the latest and greatest from Alexis King?
sentences.zh: 比如，关注 Alexis King 最新动态的最佳方式是什么？

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: I mean, the answer to is there a place that you can find all my talks is no.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关于“有没有一个地方可以找到我所有的演讲”这个问题的答案是：没有。

sentences.en: But if you are interested in following me, I have a blog, which is lexi-lambda.github.io.
sentences.zh: 但如果你有兴趣关注我，我有一个博客，地址是 lexi-lambda.github.io。

sentences.en: And also, I'm on Twitter, which is just lexi-lambda because they don't allow dashes in Twitter usernames.
sentences.zh: 此外，我还在 Twitter 上，用户名就是 lexi-lambda，因为他们不允许在 Twitter 用户名中使用连字符。

sentences.en: So, that's the main place that I post most updates.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是我发布大多数更新的主要地方。

sentences.en: The blog, honestly, I haven't written a blog post in two years.
sentences.zh: 老实说，博客我已经两年没写过文章了。

sentences.en: Hopefully, that will change soon.
sentences.zh: 希望这种情况很快会改变。

sentences.en: But there are some things there.
sentences.zh: 但上面确实有一些内容。

sentences.en: People seem to like the ones that I've written in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 人们似乎很喜欢我过去写的那几篇。

sentences.en: So, if you're interested, it's available.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你感兴趣，它就在那里。

sentences.en: Awesome.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: We will link all of that stuff in the description.
sentences.zh: 我们会把所有这些链接放在描述中。

sentences.en: Maybe I will compile a list of Alexis' greatest hits and put it in a playlist and link it in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 也许我会整理一份 Alexis 的精华合集，做成播放列表并放在节目笔记中。

sentences.en: Thanks for being on that podcast, Alexis.
sentences.zh: 感谢你参加这次播客，Alexis。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: We're back because we didn't even talk about how beautiful your slides were.
sentences.zh: 我们又回来了，因为我们甚至还没聊到你的幻灯片有多美。

sentences.en: We got carried away with the other content.
sentences.zh: 我们被其他内容带偏了。

sentences.en: Tell people quickly what...
sentences.zh: 快告诉大家……

sentences.en: And first, tell people how many slides.
sentences.zh: 首先，告诉大家有多少页幻灯片。

sentences.en: This was an hour-long keynote.
sentences.zh: 这是一场长达一小时的主讲。

sentences.en: Tell people how many slides you had and then how you made them because extremely beautiful.
sentences.zh: 告诉大家你有多少页幻灯片，以及你是怎么制作它们的，因为它们极其精美。

sentences.en: And I was halfway through the talk flabbergasted.
sentences.zh: 我在演讲进行到一半时简直惊呆了。

sentences.en: I was like, there's no way that this was manually created.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，这绝对不可能是手动创建的。

sentences.en: Something's going on here.
sentences.zh: 这里面肯定有什么名堂。

sentences.en: So, I think, I mean, if you count every individual step of every slide, there's about 300 distinct steps.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想，如果你计算每一页幻灯片的每一个独立步骤，大约有 300 个不同的步骤。

sentences.en: If you only count, you know, truly distinct slides, it's 60 slides, which is still a decent number.
sentences.zh: 如果你只计算真正不同的幻灯片，那是 60 页，这仍然是一个不错的数字。

sentences.en: You know, it's one a minute.
sentences.zh: 你知道，平均一分钟一页。

sentences.en: So, I think that's still pretty decent, pretty respectable.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这仍然相当不错，相当体面。

sentences.en: But they're all generated.
sentences.zh: 但它们全都是生成的。

sentences.en: Racket, the programming language, has a library called Hashlang Slideshow.
sentences.zh: Racket 编程语言有一个名为 Hashlang Slideshow 的库。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess it's sort of a language, but really it's just an embedded domain-specific language for making slides.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得它算是一种语言，但实际上它只是一个用于制作幻灯片的嵌入式领域特定语言。

sentences.en: And there's just sort of, there's some primitives for making different types of vector graphics, and then you can compose them together with some combinators.
sentences.zh: 它提供了一些用于制作不同类型矢量图形的原语，然后你可以用一些组合子将它们组合在一起。

sentences.en: And it's very nice.
sentences.zh: 它非常棒。

sentences.en: And, I mean, the truth is, if you just use that library, you can get some decent stuff.
sentences.zh: 而且，说实话，如果你只使用那个库，就能做出相当不错的东西。

sentences.en: But then I've also, over the years, accumulated a set of kind of additional library functions to compose things together.
sentences.zh: 但多年来，我也积累了一套额外的库函数来组合各种元素。

sentences.en: So, I'm able to just sort of say, here, I want to have this slide and have these things here, and then I just want to draw an arrow between these two things, and it'll just
sentences.zh: 所以我可以简单地说，这里，我想要这张幻灯片，放上这些东西，然后我只想在这两样东西之间画一条箭头，它就会

sentences.en: stick it there.
sentences.zh: 把它贴在那里。

sentences.en: And so, that's pretty pleasant.
sentences.zh: 所以，这非常令人愉快。

sentences.en: And I guess the most fun fact, is I was giving a talk on delimited continuations, and my library for staging slides uses delimited continuations internally.
sentences.zh: 我想最有趣的事实是，我曾经做过一次关于定界延续（delimited continuations）的演讲，而我用于演示幻灯片的库在内部正是使用了定界延续。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's just a fun meta aspect.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这只是一个有趣的元层面。

sentences.en: A fun tidbit of information.
sentences.zh: 一个有趣的小知识。

sentences.en: So, if you're not interested in learning about delimited continuations, but you are interested
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你对学习定界延续不感兴趣，但你对

sentences.en: in how to make beautiful slides, go check out the talk that's linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 如何制作精美的幻灯片感兴趣，去看看描述中链接的那个演讲吧。

sentences.en: It uses hashlang, slideshow, from the racket language.
sentences.zh: 它使用了 Racket 语言的 hashlang 和 slideshow。

sentences.en: It's a lisp.
sentences.zh: 它是一种 Lisp。

sentences.en: We all love lisps.
sentences.zh: 我们都爱 Lisp。

sentences.en: Once again, thanks for being on the pod.
sentences.zh: 再次感谢你来到播客。

sentences.en: Thank you.

sentences.en: Is that correct?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And my strategy here is like, first I read the type-driven development, uh, from Edwin Brady.
sentences.zh: 我的策略是，首先我读了 Edwin Brady 写的《类型驱动开发》。

sentences.en: That was a really good book.
sentences.zh: 那真是一本好书。

sentences.en: And after I just say, hey, let's just grab another book from my bookshelf and try to apply dependent types there and see where is actually, there are the sweet spots.
sentences.zh: 读完之后，我就想，嘿，不如从书架上再拿本书，尝试把依赖类型应用进去，看看真正的切入点在哪里。

sentences.en: Where are the sweet spots that are actually dependent types make sense and I, we don't overdo it.
sentences.zh: 看看依赖类型在哪些地方真正有意义，而且我们不会过度使用。

sentences.en: It's not painful.
sentences.zh: 这并不痛苦。

sentences.en: It's more like it's helping us.
sentences.zh: 它更多是在帮助我们。

sentences.en: Awesome.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: If people want to learn more about dependent types slash follow you on the socials, what's the best way for folks to do that?
sentences.zh: 如果人们想了解更多关于依赖类型的知识，或者在社交媒体上关注你，最好的方式是什么？

sentences.en: I have a Twitter account that we can, we can link that.
sentences.zh: 我有一个 Twitter 账号，我们可以把链接放出来。

sentences.en: Awesome.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: We will link that in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 我们会把它放在节目笔记里。

sentences.en: Anything else you want to say?
sentences.zh: 还有什么想说的吗？

sentences.en: How's, is this your first time to Lambda Days?
sentences.zh: 这是你第一次参加 Lambda Days 吗？

sentences.en: You've been here before.
sentences.zh: 你以前来过。

sentences.en: How, what are your thoughts about the conference?
sentences.zh: 你对这次会议有什么看法？

sentences.en: Uh, this is a really good conference.
sentences.zh: 呃，这是一个非常棒的会议。

sentences.en: I really like this conference because it's not really language specific.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢这个会议，因为它并不局限于某种特定语言。

sentences.en: Previously, I always attended like Haskell conferences and now this is my first real functional programming conference in the sense that there are many, so many, many
sentences.zh: 以前我总是参加像 Haskell 这样的会议，而这是我第一次真正意义上的函数式编程会议，因为这里有非常、非常多

sentences.en: functional programming languages and it's, this is a, this is something fresh for me.
sentences.zh: 函数式编程语言，这对我来说是一种新鲜的体验。

sentences.en: And this is my first time at Lambda Days.
sentences.zh: 而且这是我第一次参加 Lambda Days。

sentences.en: You think you'll be back in the future to Lambda Days 2024 or some, some version in the future?
sentences.zh: 你觉得未来还会再来参加 Lambda Days 2024 或者以后的版本吗？

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 当然会。

sentences.en: Awesome.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thanks for being on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 感谢你参加我们的播客。

sentences.en: Cheers.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: We're back with Kim.
sentences.zh: 我们又和 Kim 回来了。

sentences.en: We are going to hopefully find Becca who gave a lightning talk on functional females later to talk more about functional females.
sentences.zh: 我们希望稍后能找到 Becca，她做了一个关于“函数式女性”（Functional Females）的闪电演讲，到时候再深入聊聊这个组织。

sentences.en: But here we are standing with Kim and she mentions she's a part of the functional females organization.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们和 Kim 在一起，她提到她是“函数式女性”组织的成员。

sentences.en: I'm not sure as an organizer or as a member.
sentences.zh: 我不确定她是组织者还是普通成员。

sentences.en: So tell us a bit about functional females and how other conferences can get involved or have them involved in their conference.
sentences.zh: 那么跟我们聊聊“函数式女性”吧，其他会议该如何参与，或者如何让她们参与到会议中来？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So I am not an organizer.
sentences.zh: 我不是组织者。

sentences.en: Becca and Liv are the organizers.
sentences.zh: Becca 和 Liv 才是组织者。

sentences.en: Full credit to them.
sentences.zh: 功劳全归她们。

sentences.en: They did a great job setting it up.
sentences.zh: 她们把这个组织建立得非常好。

sentences.en: It's very, very new.
sentences.zh: 它非常、非常新。

sentences.en: It launched about two months ago and I am a community lead for the
sentences.zh: 大约两个月前才成立，我是该组织

sentences.en: Scala community.
sentences.zh: Scala 社区的负责人。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: And is this a global organization or is it based mostly in Europe?
sentences.zh: 这是一个全球性的组织，还是主要在欧洲？

sentences.en: Because I'd never heard about them before attending this conference today or and yesterday.
sentences.zh: 因为在参加今天和昨天的会议之前，我从未听说过她们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So far, I think all the members are Europe-based.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，我想所有成员都位于欧洲。

sentences.en: It's about 70 women so far that work in various functional programming languages and so far are all based in Europe.
sentences.zh: 目前大约有 70 位女性，她们使用各种函数式编程语言，目前都身处欧洲。

sentences.en: But I don't think it's a requirement to be based in Europe.
sentences.zh: 但我认为身处欧洲并不是加入的必要条件。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: So I'm primarily a member of the C++ community.
sentences.zh: 我主要是 C++ 社区的成员。

sentences.en: Would functional females be interested in entering C++?
sentences.zh: “函数式女性”有兴趣进入 C++ 领域吗？

sentences.en: Because we got some functional stuff or are you guys trying to stick to like the Lambda Days, you know, Zuri Hack, I don't know all the functional conferences.
sentences.zh: 因为我们也有一些函数式的东西，或者你们只是想坚持像 Lambda Days、Zuri Hack 这种，我不知道所有的函数式会议。

sentences.en: What's the main sort of vision of functional females?
sentences.zh: “函数式女性”的主要愿景是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: As far as I know, we're not really into C++.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，我们并没有真正涉足 C++。

sentences.en: We have, yeah, Scala is the largest group so far.
sentences.zh: 我们有，是的，Scala 是目前最大的小组。

sentences.en: So we're very focused on Scala events.
sentences.zh: 所以我们非常专注于 Scala 活动。

sentences.en: Also Elixir and RuSt. And yeah, just functional conferences like this one.
sentences.zh: 还有 Elixir 和 Rust。是的，就是像这样的函数式会议。

sentences.en: Wait, you guys are interested in Rust, but not C++?
sentences.zh: 等等，你们对 Rust 感兴趣，但对 C++ 不感兴趣？

sentences.en: What's going on here?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Talk to Becca and Liv.
sentences.zh: 去问问 Becca 和 Liv 吧。

sentences.en: We will find Becca and Liv, and we will get to the bottom of this, folks.
sentences.zh: 我们会找到 Becca 和 Liv，查个水落石出，各位。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Thanks, Kim, for being on the pod for the third time.
sentences.zh: 谢谢 Kim 第三次参加我们的播客。

sentences.en: Enjoy the rest of your dessert.
sentences.zh: 好好享受剩下的甜点吧。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I just keep coming back for more.
sentences.zh: 我总是忍不住想再来。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We're here.
sentences.zh: 我们到了。

sentences.en: We're back.
sentences.zh: 我们回来了。

sentences.en: We're interviewing Lambda Days 2023, day two.
sentences.zh: 我们正在采访 Lambda Days 2023 的第二天。

sentences.en: We're here with Pierre.
sentences.zh: 我们和 Pierre 在一起。

sentences.en: Am I pronouncing that correctly?
sentences.zh: 我发音正确吗？

sentences.en: Pierre.
sentences.zh: Pierre。

sentences.en: Pierre.
sentences.zh: Pierre。

sentences.en: But I listen to Pierre, too.
sentences.zh: 但我听起来也像 Peter。

sentences.en: You listen?
sentences.zh: 你听到了？

sentences.en: I mean...
sentences.zh: 我是说……

sentences.en: Because the English speakers say Pierre.
sentences.zh: 因为讲英语的人都说 Pierre。

sentences.en: It's better than Peter that I was calling you for like the first couple hours when I...
sentences.zh: 这比我前几个小时一直叫你 Peter 要好，当时我……

sentences.en: Everything works.
sentences.zh: 怎么叫都行。

sentences.en: Everything works.
sentences.zh: 怎么叫都行。

sentences.en: Pierre, Peter, whatever.
sentences.zh: Pierre，Peter，都一样。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So most of the folks won't know you.
sentences.zh: 大多数人可能不认识你。

sentences.en: Introduce yourself.
sentences.zh: 自我介绍一下吧。

sentences.en: Where are you from?
sentences.zh: 你来自哪里？

sentences.en: What company do you work for?
sentences.zh: 你在哪家公司工作？

sentences.en: And sort of what technologies are you working with?
sentences.zh: 以及你主要使用什么技术？

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: The whole name is Pierre Stritzinger, which is also the name of my company.
sentences.zh: 全名是 Pierre Stritzinger，这也是我公司的名字。

sentences.en: And we basically run Erlang directly on hardware.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上是直接在硬件上运行 Erlang。

sentences.en: And that's what I've been presenting on here several times in the paSt. And this time I was lazy and didn't submit the talk.
sentences.zh: 这也是我过去几次在这里演讲的主题。这次我偷懒了，没提交演讲。

sentences.en: And I'm just like hanging around.
sentences.zh: 我就在这儿随便逛逛。

sentences.en: You did give a lightning talk today.
sentences.zh: 你今天确实做了一个闪电演讲。

sentences.en: You wasn't completely lazy.
sentences.zh: 你并没有完全偷懒。

sentences.en: Tell us what you talked about in the lightning talk.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们你在闪电演讲里讲了什么。

sentences.en: In the lightning talk, I just gave the Grisp roadmap of what we're up to.
sentences.zh: 在闪电演讲中，我只是介绍了 Grisp 的路线图，说明我们正在做什么。

sentences.en: Basically, so we built hardware to actually run, make it easier for other people to run it on the hardware.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我们制造硬件，是为了让其他人更容易地在硬件上运行它。

sentences.en: So we can actually provide a better user experience.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就能提供更好的用户体验。

sentences.en: And I gave the roadmap of the next things to come, like little hardware sensor modules that we are building to plug into the main board, a battery board,
sentences.zh: 我介绍了接下来的计划，比如我们正在制造的小型硬件传感器模块，可以插入主板，还有电池板，

sentences.en: like a charger board and also Grisp Zero, which will be the new thing, which will be the smallest thing that will be running the full-blown Erlang VM.
sentences.zh: 充电板，以及 Grisp Zero，这将是新的产品，也是运行完整 Erlang VM 的最小设备。

sentences.en: And if I recall correctly in the talk, you mentioned that the Zero was inspired by the Raspberry Pi Zero, which I don't know much about.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，你在演讲中提到 Zero 的灵感来自 Raspberry Pi Zero，我对那个不太了解。

sentences.en: But so what's the sort of difference?
sentences.zh: 那么它们之间有什么区别呢？

sentences.en: Or is there a comparison between the Raspberry Pi and Grisp?
sentences.zh: 或者说 Raspberry Pi 和 Grisp 之间有可比性吗？

sentences.en: Or are they completely different?
sentences.zh: 还是说它们完全不同？

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全不同。

sentences.en: I just stole the name.
sentences.zh: 我只是借用了这个名字。

sentences.en: And so tell us a bit more about Grisp.
sentences.zh: 那么再跟我们多聊聊 Grisp 吧。

sentences.en: So if people are interested in acquiring this hardware, is it something that people can use for hobby projects?
sentences.zh: 如果人们有兴趣购买这种硬件，它是可以用于业余项目吗？

sentences.en: Or is it used by sort of big companies?
sentences.zh: 还是说它被大公司使用？

sentences.en: What do folks use the hardware for?
sentences.zh: 大家用这个硬件做什么？

sentences.en: So the hardware and the software stack, because the software stack is actually the more important thing.
sentences.zh: 硬件和软件栈，因为软件栈其实更重要。

sentences.en: The hardware is just an evaluation board to actually try it out.
sentences.zh: 硬件只是一个用来试用的评估板。

sentences.en: It's used by industry.
sentences.zh: 它被工业界使用。

sentences.en: As I know of, mainly by us, also for developing our own products.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，主要是我们自己在用，也用于开发我们自己的产品。

sentences.en: It's used by a lot of universities for teaching, because it's more fun for the professor not to have to read half of the master's thesis about, like,
sentences.zh: 很多大学用它来教学，因为教授们不用再读一半关于如何让 Raspberry Pi 运行 Erlang 并点亮一个小灯的硕士论文，这会更有趣，

sentences.en: how to get a Raspberry Pi working with Erlang and having a bit switched on, because that's always the same.
sentences.zh: 因为那总是千篇一律的。

sentences.en: Because this, kind of like the zero-to-blinking light, we actually can provide in 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 因为这种“从零到点亮小灯”的过程，我们实际上可以在 10 分钟内完成。

sentences.en: And then you start to do fun stuff.
sentences.zh: 然后你就可以开始做有趣的事情了。

sentences.en: And it's also used by hobbyists for all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 它也被业余爱好者用于各种各样的项目。

sentences.en: Awesome.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So I'll be sure to find links that we can put in the show notes if people are interested in checking this out.
sentences.zh: 如果人们有兴趣查看这些内容，我一定会找到链接放在节目笔记里。

sentences.en: If people don't know much about Erlang, because I think most of our listeners are sort of in the C++ space, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果人们对 Erlang 不太了解，因为我想我们的听众大多是在 C++ 领域，你知道，

sentences.en: give us like a 30-second overview of Erlang and why people might be interested in Erlang and not Elixir.
sentences.zh: 给我们做一个 30 秒的 Erlang 概述，以及为什么人们可能对 Erlang 感兴趣而不是 Elixir。

sentences.en: Because we talked to Jose Valim earlier, and, you know, he's the creator of the Elixir language, which is built on top of the Beam.
sentences.zh: 因为我们之前和 Jose Valim 聊过，他是 Elixir 语言的创造者，该语言构建在 BEAM 之上。

sentences.en: Anyways, I'll let you talk about Erlang and why people might be interested.
sentences.zh: 总之，还是让你来谈谈 Erlang 以及为什么人们会感兴趣吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So the Beam is the common virtual machine that we share.
sentences.zh: BEAM 是我们共享的通用虚拟机。

sentences.en: Well, actually, Elixir is not, like, based on the Beam, but actually based on Erlang.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实 Elixir 并不是基于 BEAM，而是基于 Erlang。

sentences.en: It's running on top of Erlang.
sentences.zh: 它运行在 Erlang 之上。

sentences.en: So without Erlang, Elixir would not be there.
sentences.zh: 所以没有 Erlang，就不会有 Elixir。

sentences.en: So Erlang is basically the base technology, the older language.
sentences.zh: 所以 Erlang 基本上是基础技术，是更古老的语言。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, if you like Ruby syntax more, use Elixir.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你更喜欢 Ruby 的语法，那就用 Elixir。

sentences.en: If you like Prolog syntax more, you don't care about syntax, use Elixir.
sentences.zh: 如果你更喜欢 Prolog 的语法，那你其实根本不在乎语法，用 Elixir 就行。

sentences.en: It's more kind of like, it is older, but it's also more kind of like to the ground, what the actual virtual machine does.
sentences.zh: 它更像是……虽然它比较老，但它也更贴近底层，更接近虚拟机的实际运作方式。

sentences.en: So the unique selling point, why you want to use it, or both languages, is it's the only systems that allow full Torrent prograMs.
sentences.zh: 所以它独特的卖点，或者说你为什么想用它，又或者说这两门语言的卖点，在于它是唯一允许实现全容错程序的系统。

sentences.en: So your software has bugs, but your code keeps running and working.
sentences.zh: 所以即使你的软件有 Bug，你的代码也能持续运行并正常工作。

sentences.en: And there's a pretty big company that was acquired, what was it, for $20 billion, $30 billion, that we were talking about last night.
sentences.zh: 而且有一家规模相当大的公司被收购了，是多少来着，200 亿还是 300 亿美元，我们昨晚还聊到过。

sentences.en: Oh, you mean WhatsApp, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，你是说 WhatsApp，对吧。

sentences.en: Oh, it's run everywhere.
sentences.zh: 哦，它无处不在。

sentences.en: Basically, there was an estimate once that 95% of the human communication goes over a system with Erlang at some point.
sentences.zh: 基本上，曾经有人估计，人类 95% 的通信在某个环节都会经过使用 Erlang 的系统。

sentences.en: So that includes all the Erickson base stations.
sentences.zh: 这包括了所有的爱立信基站。

sentences.en: All Cisco switches have Erlang in them.
sentences.zh: 所有的思科交换机里都有 Erlang。

sentences.en: WhatsApp has Erlang in them.
sentences.zh: WhatsApp 里也有 Erlang。

sentences.en: And then probably you're already in 95%.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能已经在那个 95% 的范围内了。

sentences.en: Oh, I had no idea.
sentences.zh: 哦，我完全不知道。

sentences.en: I knew about the WhatsApp story.
sentences.zh: 我知道 WhatsApp 的故事。

sentences.en: I had no idea about the other stuff.
sentences.zh: 但我对其他这些一无所知。

sentences.en: Erlang is used for a lot of infrastructure stuff and is hidden in a lot of places where people don't know it, where people actually need this robustness.
sentences.zh: Erlang 被用于许多基础设施，隐藏在很多人们不知道的地方，而那些地方恰恰需要这种稳健性。

sentences.en: For example, all the banks use Erlang for trading.
sentences.zh: 例如，所有的银行都使用 Erlang 进行交易。

sentences.en: They just don't talk about it, so we don't know.
sentences.zh: 他们只是不谈论它，所以我们不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, we know in the Erlang community, but it's not official.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们在 Erlang 社区里是知道的，但这并不是官方公开的。

sentences.en: They don't talk about it.
sentences.zh: 他们不会谈论这个。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: I'm going to have to find some links to link in the show notes, because I know a little bit about Erlang, but not that it's used globally around the world.
sentences.zh: 我得找些链接放到节目备注里，因为我虽然了解一点 Erlang，但不知道它在全球范围内被应用得这么广泛。

sentences.en: Last thing I'll ask, I believe, if I recall correctly from last night, you have been attending Lambda Days for a very long time, if not from the get-go.
sentences.zh: 最后一个问题，如果我昨晚没记错的话，你应该参加 Lambda Days 很久了，甚至可能从一开始就在参加。

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: I think I missed the first one.
sentences.zh: 我想我错过了第一届。

sentences.en: I think my first one was the second one, and there was the break during the pandemic, and I couldn't have attended last year, but I was at all others.
sentences.zh: 我参加的第一届应该是第二届，中间因为疫情中断过，去年我也没能参加，但其他的我都参加了。

sentences.en: And so you've been a long-time attendee, keep coming back.
sentences.zh: 所以你是一位资深参会者，一直都在回来参加。

sentences.en: Why is Lambda Days so awesome?
sentences.zh: 为什么 Lambda Days 这么棒？

sentences.en: And if someone's thinking about coming to Lambda Days in the future, what would you tell them?
sentences.zh: 如果有人在考虑将来参加 Lambda Days，你会对他们说什么？

sentences.en: I mean, if you are into functional programming, or you want to find out about functional programming, because both works very well, Lambda Days is a very good place to be.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你对函数式编程感兴趣，或者想了解函数式编程，因为这两者在这里都非常合适，Lambda Days 是一个非常好的去处。

sentences.en: It's a great conference.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很棒的会议。

sentences.en: They have so great content.
sentences.zh: 他们的内容非常精彩。

sentences.en: I always come home with ideas.
sentences.zh: 我每次回家都能带回一些新想法。

sentences.en: And it's not like a theoretical conference, like ICFP, functional programming, like academic conference.
